content.p: This Act is the Emergency Response Fund Amendment (Disaster Ready Fund) Act 2022.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

The day this Act receives the Royal Assent.

A single day to be fixed by Proclamation. However, if the provisions do not commence within the period of 6 months beginning on the day this Act receives the Royal Assent, they commence on the day after the end of that period.

content.p: Note: This table relates only to the provisions of this Act as originally enacted. It will not be amended to deal with any later amendments of this Act.
Any information in column 3 of the table is not part of this Act. Information may be inserted in this column, or information in it may be edited, in any published version of this Act.

Legislation that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

section.heading: Consequential amendments of the Emergency Response Fund Investment Mandate Direction 2020

content.p: During the period:
beginning at the commencement of this section; and
ending immediately before the commencement of Schedule 1 to this Act;
the responsible Ministers may, by legislative instrument, make the following amendments of the Emergency Response Fund Investment Mandate Direction 2020:
(c) in section 1 of that Direction, omitting “Emergency Response Fund” and substituting “Disaster Ready Fund”;
(d) in section 3 of that Direction, omitting “made under the Emergency Response Fund Act 2019” and substituting “in force under the Disaster Ready Fund Act 2019”;
(e) in the definition of Act in section 4 of that Direction, omitting “Emergency Response Fund Act 2019” and substituting “Disaster Ready Fund Act 2019”;
(f) in the definition of Fund in section 4 of that Direction, omitting “Emergency Response Fund” and substituting “Disaster Ready Fund”.
An instrument made under subsection (1) of this section must not take effect before the commencement of Schedule 1 to this Act.

(3) Section 42 of the Emergency Response Fund Act 2019 (which deals with consultation) applies to the making of an instrument under subsection (1) of this section in a corresponding way to the way in which it applies to the giving of a direction under subsection 39(1) of that Act.
(4) This section does not, by implication, limit the application of subsection 33(3) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 to any other power to make an instrument.
(5) For the purposes of this section, responsible Ministers has the same meaning as in the Emergency Response Fund Act 2019.

section.heading: Annual report regarding arrangements and grants

content.p: The Emergency Management Minister must cause to be prepared, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, an annual report on the exercise of the Minister’s functions and powers under section 20 (which deals with arrangements and grants) during the year.

Without limiting subsection (1), the report must include the following in relation to each process by which a decision was made during the year to make one or more section 20 arrangements or section 20 grants:
details of how the process was conducted;
for each arrangement or grant that was made as a result of the process:
the name of the person (other than an individual) or body with or to which the arrangement or grant was made; and
details of the arrangement or grant made;
for each person or body that, as part of the process, made an unsuccessful application (however described) for an arrangement or grant:
the name of the person (other than an individual) or body; and
details of the arrangement or grant applied for.
However, information described in paragraph (2)(c) can only be included in the report if the person or body that made the unsuccessful application provides their agreement in writing.

The Emergency Management Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the end of the financial year to which the report relates.
The Emergency Management Minister must cause an independent review of the following matters to be undertaken before the fifth anniversary of the commencement of this section:
the section 20 arrangements and section 20 grants that have been made, including their purposes and the payments made in relation to them;
the appropriateness of the processes by which decisions to make or not to make such arrangements and grants have been made, taking into account the information reported under section 26A;

(c) the implementation of any guidelines for making decisions of that kind, and compliance with the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 and instruments made under that Act in relation to those decisions;
whether any additional measures should be taken (including amendments of this Act) to improve transparency relating to decisions of that kind, and if so what those measures should be.
The person or persons who conduct the review must:
give the Emergency Management Minister a written report of the review; and
do so before the fifth anniversary of the commencement of this section.
The Emergency Management Minister must cause a copy of:
the terms of reference for the review; and
the report of the review;
to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is given to the Minister.
The Emergency Management Minister must also cause a copy of the terms of reference and report to be published on the NEMA’s website as soon as practicable after the report is given to the Minister.

division.heading: Limitation on total annual debits from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account

section.heading: Limitation on total annual debits from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account

content.p: The total amount debited from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account under sections 28A and 32A during:
the financial year beginning on 1 July 2023; or
a later financial year;
must not exceed:
$200 million; or
if another amount is applicable to the financial year in accordance with subsection (2) or (3)—that other amount.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), the responsible Ministers may, by legislative instrument, determine the amount applicable to:
a specified financial year; and
each subsequent financial year.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d), the responsible Ministers may, by legislative instrument, determine:
one or more financial years; and
for each of those financial years—the amount applicable to the financial year concerned.
A determination under subsection (2) does not apply to a financial year that is covered by a determination under subsection (3).
In making a determination under subsection (2) or (3), the responsible Ministers must have regard to:

the advice given by the Future Fund Board under section 34A in relation to the impact of the making of the determination on the ability of the Future Fund Board to comply with this Act and the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate; and
such other matters (if any) as the responsible Ministers consider relevant.
Financial year beginning on 1 July 2022
The total amount debited from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account under sections 28 and 32 during the financial year beginning on 1 July 2022 must not exceed $150 million.
The total amount debited from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account under sections 28A and 32A during the financial year beginning on 1 July 2022 must not exceed $50 million.
Review
At least once every 5 years, the responsible Ministers must conduct a review of the operation of paragraphs (1)(c) and (d).

section.heading: Determinations—advice given by the Future Fund Board

content.p: Before making a determination under subsection 34(2) or (3), the responsible Ministers must give the Future Fund Board a written notice that:
sets out a draft of the determination; and
requires the Future Fund Board to:
give advice to those Ministers about the impact of the making of the determination on the ability of the Future Fund Board to comply with this Act and the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate; and
do so within the period specified in the notice; and
requires the Future Fund Board, in giving that advice, to have regard to:
the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate; and
such other matters (if any) as are specified in the notice.
The Future Fund Board must comply with a requirement in a notice under subsection (1).
A period specified under subparagraph (1)(b)(ii) must not be shorter than 60 days after the notice is given.
A matter specified under subparagraph (1)(c)(ii) must not be inconsistent with:
this Act; or
the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate.
Paragraph (1)(c) does not, by implication, limit the matters to which the Future Fund Board may have regard.
The advice given by the Future Fund Board in accordance with subparagraph (1)(b)(i) must be tabled in each House of the Parliament with the relevant determination.
Note: As the determination is a legislative instrument, it is also tabled in each House of the Parliament under section 38 of the Legislation Act 2003.

the repeal of that subsection by this Schedule does not affect the continuity of the arrangement; and
